notes: Early-stage evaluation for embedding a low-latency streaming copilot into FleetCraft's hosted IDE. Primary ask: consistent Time-To-First-Token (TTFT) and controlled token-budget behaviour for long-lived editor sessions. Engineering-led conversations (CTO + platform eng). Key constraints: must hit interactive TTFT targets on developer machines across NA regions, support graceful degradation/backpressure rather than hard failures, and provide model/version pinning per customer and per-route. Interested in Redwood's dedicated pools + Optimize recommendations for token tuning. Quote from CTO: 'We need suggestions to start flowing in <80ms for the majority of sessions; spikes are fine only if we can fall back smoothly.'
use_case_summary: FleetCraft plans to ship an in-editor copiloting feature (real-time completions + multi-turn assistant) where the UX depends on sub-100ms TTFT, predictable jitter, and a token budget model that prevents runaway costs for long sessions. They require streaming SDK support with chunked incremental responses, backpressure hooks into the editor to avoid bursty token overage, per-workspace model pinning, and clear metrics for p50/p95 TTFT and jitter. POC will instrument prefix/KV cache reuse and quantized model variants for cost/latency trade-offs.
